text:
sara (AE): quick heads-up — Nimbly demo tomorrow 10am PST. during their trial they got a bunch of 429s against /v1/generate. Requesting a short write-up on our rate profile and a temporary fix we can apply for the demo. can someone confirm cause?

miguel (Eng): do you have sample logs or a request id? is it per-route 429 or account-level?

sara (AE): pasted a snippet from their test run: ```
2026-03-20T18:02:03Z ERROR request_id=ry7Gf 429 Too Many Requests route=/v1/generate tenant=acme-nimbly tokens=342 seq_len=512
2026-03-20T18:02:03Z WARN token_bucket=exhausted tenant=acme-nimbly burst_window=60s allowed=120 used=121
```

miguel (Eng): looks like the per-tenant token bucket was exhausted (used>allowed) inside the 60s burst window. their workload is spiky — many heavy seqs. not a model latency issue.

jamie (SRE): to add — we have two layers: global account quota + per-route/per-tenant burst caps. the logs show token_bucket exhaustion at the tenant level. quick mitigation options: 1) temporary per-route burst increase for the demo (1h) 2) route-level reservation (reserve X tokens) 3) throttle client SDK to smooth spikes.

tina (SE): client side change might be harder before demo. can we do an infra-side short bump so the demo doesn't fail? also sales asked for a one-paragraph explanation to send to customer.

miguel (Eng): yes we can bump per-route burst window and allowed tokens for tenant `acme-nimbly` on hosted for 1 hour. I'll need the exact tenant id and demo window.

sara (AE): tenant id is acme-nimbly, demo 2026-03-21 10:00-10:30 PST. can you do a 2x burst allowance?

jamie (SRE): scheduling now — applying `per_route.burst_allowed=240` (was 120) for tenant `acme-nimbly` for 45 minutes starting 2026-03-21T17:45Z. infra-bot will post update.

infra-bot: applied config change id cfg_9a3bf, eviction=off, effective=2026-03-21T17:45Z, expires=2026-03-21T18:30Z :white_check_mark:

miguel (Eng): also enabling temporary metrics alert with 2x threshold for that tenant so we can rollback if error rate spikes unexpectedly.

tina (SE): short explanation for customer: "We enforce per-tenant token budgets and short burst windows to protect shared capacity. Your demo workload produced short spikes of long generations that exceeded the tenant burst allowance, causing 429s. For the demo we temporarily increased your per-route burst allowance to avoid interruptions while we work with you on a smoothing strategy (client-side backoff, smaller seqs, or a reserved capacity plan)." feel free to tweak.

sara (AE): perfect, sending that now. any follow-up actions?

miguel (Eng): follow-up: capture a 30-min trace during demo, then review their seq_len distribution. recommend one of: (A) tune client to cap concurrent long seqs, (B) enable prefix KV caching if they repeat prompts, (C) move to Dedicated or reserve-ahead if steady high throughput.

jamie (SRE): I'll revert the burst bump at expiry and confirm. will also leave a note in the tenant config: "temporary demo increase applied by jamie (SRE) — monitor & revert"

sara (AE): thanks everyone — huge help. :raised_hands: I'll update the customer and loop back after demo with notes.

miguel (Eng): noted. ping here with the demo trace id and we'll do a quick post-mortem tomorrow.

sara (AE): will do — closing this thread for now, re-open after demo if anything else crops up.
